Variants.Content: The value of a castle in Westeros lies not only in high walls, but in wells, granaries, stables, artisans, bows and crossbows, gates, and the roads by which relief forces might arrive. Besiegers may use trebuchets, scaling ladders, siege towers, boiling oil, mines, blockades, and terms of surrender; defenders rely on high walls, stored grain, troop rotation, morale, and waiting for outside relief. To lords, a siege is a contest of legal right and supply; to common folk inside the walls, fortifications mean shelter, and may also mean a long wait crowded together in hunger and disease.
